The game is good, BUT... I'm really tired of using that But nowadays...
I will start with the negative because it frustrated me.
So, the game has performance issues. On the bigger cinematics it has huge FPS drops and lags.
It is super unhinged. I used my AMD adrenaline to lock the fps at 60 for smoother gameplay. But during cinematics... it goes from 120 to 300 with vsync on. And from 500 to 1000 with vsync off. Cringe.
But the main problem isn't the fps, it is the drops and it's super annoying.
So, I went to forums and found that lots of people got the same problem. Most of the conversations were from around 3 years ago... still not fixed. Cringe x2. Shame on the devs.

This is the solution (not mine, but it helped):

- in-game, make sure to select the Fullscreen display option (so not borderless, or windowed). Now exit the game.
- go to the install directory (by default, this is: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\KingdomComeDeliverance)
- make a new file called user.cfg, place it in the install directory
- open the new file in notepad
- write the following in the file:

r_VSync = 0
sys_MaxFPS = 60 (or depending on your monitor)

About the good things. Well, I only played around 3h. The game is kinda slow at start. Didn't see much of it yet, but it looks beautiful and the characters feel alive. The story is good so far. I plan on playing more... hope I don't reach another stupid performance things.
Overall it's worth. And the game is really good. But I am not going to sugar coat it when the devs are that lazy...

The graphics aren't the greatest, the combat is clunky and feels like 'wood', the npcs look like clay, when you fight more than 1 enemy you get assr*ped. Apart from that, it's not a bad game by any means just that I kind of ruined for myself by playing KCD2 before KCD.

citations.review_text:
Kingdom Come: Deliverance is an amazing RPG, but its flaws overshadow the incredible potential it had.
The first issue is the game's incredibly slow pacing, which severely limits how I explore the world. There are very few basic QOL features, making the game feel frustrating rather than genuinely challenging.
There are still bugs in some of the long quests that forced me to reload old saves just to fix them. The camera works terribly during many people fights, and the hitboxes in some of the main story battles are also inconsistent. Worst of all is the save system. The lack of a proper autosave system is one of the game's biggest flaws.

That said, the game has some obvious strengths. The graphics are beautiful, the RPG progression system gives you a strong sense of growth, and the questlines along with the different ways you can approach them. The combat system is fantastic and constantly made me want to find more people to fight... as long as it's a 1v1, lmao.

After about 40 hours, I've decided it's better to uninstall the game, watch the rest of the story on youtube, and move on to Kingdom Come: Deliverance II before I end up hating this one.

7/10. If the developers fixed the issues that really shouldn't have been, this game would easily deserve a 9/10.

Nice voice-acting, music, fun activities and side quests await you. the devs really had an eye for detail. The combat system took some time to get used to, but when you master it, it gets super easy. thats the only twist i remember. especially if its a little later in the game and you got armor and stuff.. only thing thats challenging is if they are rushing you with 4-5 people at once. if you want a nice medieval story, i can easily recommend buying this game!

the game is very good and realistic, you can`t rush things you need to chill and learn how to fight, how to pickpocket, how to do poisons and more. the combat alone carries this game, i really like how the combat works and how you need to focus on the enemies one by one while watching the surrounding area, and the skills in the game are great, there are plenty of skills to learn, the way you level up skills is even greater, to level a skill you just use it, so you start as a weak beta who can`t carry a bow properly to becoming Hanzo, there is plenty of main and side quests to do, a lot of heretics to kill, and many places to visit, the graphics are super good for a 2018 game, there are plenty of armour and clothing pieces to wear, a lot of houses and churches to steal from, you can steal everything and anything in this game even the monastery! what a cool game design.

saving: the saving is one of the most frustrating things in the game can`t save whenever you want, you need a special item to save or to go to your main bed and sleep to save, i hate it a lot but i got used to it after like 20 hours.

I gave up on this game originally when I first bought it because the "tutorial" frustrated me beyond reason, and I had just come off playing other medieval games like Mount and Blade, and Mordhau, I thought maybe I was just stuck in a mode that didn't favor KCD1's style of gameplay, so I put it off. My latest experience has gone a little more tolerably, but only a little. I am trying to let it grow on me, but I do not see myself finishing this game. I don't really even see myself finishing this quest. Usually my ego kicks in at a point like this and I force myself to play a game because maybe I'm just bad and I just need to getgud, but unlike soulsborne games or other medieval combat games, I feel absolutely nothing for the idea of getting "good enough" to finish KCD1.

The combat is truly an awful experience. Interesting concept, HORRIBLE application. They teach you how to do attack combos, block, parry, do feints, and the combat wheel is cool and all, but all the mechanics are designed for one-on-one combat, which is non-applicable to most of the scenarios you will find yourself in if you pursue the main quest. Furthermore, and most importantly: Any enemy that isn't a threadbare, half-dead bandit will "master strike" you to death if you try to attack them normally. Everything you learned about fighting in KCD1 can be tossed out the window the moment you learn master strike, because it is the only way to win battles.
 I'm not even being hyperbolic, the enemy NPC's will absolutely slaughter you if you try attacks and do combos, and not just spam master strikes instead. Master strikes are a timed, single button press "parry and strike" attack that is unblockable, and primed by an attacker swinging their weapon at the user. Essentially, you learn to stop attacking, and just wait for enemies to attack you, because there's no point to doing anything else.

KCD was a rollercoaster ride for me. It had very high ups, but unfortunately equally low downs. The RPG aspects with npcs moving around the game world, having their own schedule can breathe so much life into a game like this. On the other hand, it went a bit too hardcore when the game asks you to find certain npcs to progress, but they put no marker and with the dynamic nature of the game, it can be very frustrating to find a particular npc tied to a quest because they moved on due to certain world condition. A bit more information would have helped a long way here.

The voice acting and open world design is good, there is not much to explore beyond the towns, but the world design feels the most realistic depiction of a medieval Europe I've ever seen. Despite being a 2018 game, this game holds up really well! Made using Cryengine, game has vritually no stutter and lighting and detail is extremely impressive.

There are some really bad parts of the game which makes the review complicated, let's start with the combat. After spending hours upon hours learning the combat, even going out of the game to watch videos online, it never felt good. It works ok on 1v1 encounter, but the combat system breaks down fast when you engage multiple foes at once, it feels so clumsy and derpy. I love their idea of a more tactical and 'realistic' take on combat, but it never felt right.

Then there is a one particular point in the story which was so frustrating as the game confines you to a single building. In reality the premise and options you a seamingly given sounds so amazing, I got really excited. In execution however, it was the most frustrating moment of the game to the point I felt like I wanted to drop this game.

All this making KCD a very complicated game to review. On one hand, I had the most immersive, addictive  experience I can have with a video game. On the other hand, it can be one of the most frustrating as well. It depends on whether you have the patience to p…

Everything is great except the most important feature. COMPAT its so awful that I cant even begin to describe it. So buggy, not responsive, and designed for 1v1 only. The moment you have 2 npcs or more you're done for. Also it's such a great idea to give npc the ability to perfectly block everything you attack. You'd ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spend 10mins in a fight and do absolutely no damage.

EDIT: Ok maybe it's not tooo bad, combat still annoying but manageable when you get used to it. Still it took me around 25hrs just to finally start having fun at combat

**Recommended**

I went into *Kingdom Come: Deliverance* expecting a medieval RPG, but what I got was a game that fully commits to realism—for better and worse.

The world is one of the most immersive I've experienced. Villages feel alive, forests are beautiful, and NPCs follow believable daily routines. The story is grounded, and watching Henry grow from an ordinary blacksmith's son into a capable fighter is genuinely rewarding.

That said, this game isn't for everyone. Combat has a steep learning curve and can feel frustrating at first. Saving is limited, lockpicking is difficult early on, and the pacing is much slower than most modern RPGs. If you're expecting something like Skyrim, you'll probably be disappointed.

However, if you're willing to learn the mechanics and embrace the slower pace, the game becomes incredibly satisfying. Every victory feels earned, every piece of armor matters, and even simple tasks like preparing for a journey add to the immersion.

**Pros:**

* Beautiful and believable medieval world
* Excellent quest design with multiple solutions
* Strong historical atmosphere
* Rewarding character progression

**Cons:**

* Steep learning curve
* Clunky combat early on
* Some bugs and rough edges remain
* Slow pacing may not appeal to everyone

Overall, *Kingdom Come: Deliverance* is a unique RPG that respects the player's patience instead of holding their hand. It has flaws, but its strengths easily outweigh them if you're looking for an immersive medieval experience.

This game is an absolute work of art. While the punishing and occasionally strange game mechanics might not appeal to everyone, if you give it time, you'll overcome these challenges and truly fall in love with it.

[h2] Pros: [/h2]
• [b] Atmosphere. [/b] This is exactly what a medieval game should be. Authentic world-building, historical locations, accurate architecture, and well-developed characters make this game one of a kind. You can genuinely learn about the period just by playing and observing  people.
• [b] Story and quests. [/b] Every mission and quest is carefully designed to immerse you without feeling overwhelmed. The entire plot is interconnected: actions taken in earlier missions can affect (or even lock you out of) quests later on. Multiple story paths branch based on your choices throughout the entire playthrough. Additionally, most missions feature optional tasks focused on immersion, allowing you to either savor the storyline or rush through it at your own pace.
• [b] Realism. [/b] While some might see this as a downside, I found immense fun in navigating the unusual mechanics that intentionally slow down the gameplay. From early on, you have to manually learn how to perform almost everything, which is rare compared to modern RPGs. The steep learning curve, complex (and sometimes clunky) combat system, slow skill progression, gear maintenance, and reputation system will either captivate you immediately or drive away casual gamers. To top it off, Hardcore Mode adds even more depth, demanding even more strategy and patience.

The biggest complaint about this game is easily the combat, and even I have to admit it is clunky at times. 

But if anyone tells you that it is the absolute worst thing in the world, they're either:

~Just not good at the game.

~Not training their combat skills enough.

~Trying to fight a 1v5.

Remember that this game's main gimmick is being brutally realistic. If you try to fight against even 2 dudes at a time and they have better kits than you, then you will most likely get your ass whooped, ESPECIALLY at earlier stages of the game.

Here are some tips for combat so that you don't end up in the reviews typing about how this game's combat is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing of all time:

~DON'T FIGHT LARGE GROUPS! With the right equipment (and skill) you can pull off a 1v2, or even a 1v3. But 1v4 is where it starts to get risky.

~Never go into a fight tired or hungry. Both of those lower your stats and possibly cause you to die.

~Train. You have to train with Bernard. It might be a boring slog, but you have to train if you don't want to get killed by the first bandit you see. Train until you hit level 3 with your selected weapon, and then learn 
master-strikes. (aka the most op mechanic in the game)

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is one of the most immersive RPGs I've ever played.

This isn't a power fantasy. You start as an ordinary blacksmith's son who can barely hold a sword, and every improvement feels earned. Learning to fight, read, brew potions, and survive in medieval Bohemia creates a level of immersion that very few RPGs can match. The world is believable, the combat is rewarding once mastered, and every mechanic exists to make you feel like you're truly living in the 15th century.

Unfortunately, the quest design doesn't live up to the same standard.

Too many quests, both main and side, follow a very similar formula: investigate, ride across the map, talk to several NPCs, investigate again, then report back. The lack of variety gradually hurts the pacing, and by the final act I found myself rushing through the main story because I simply couldn't stay invested in the quest structure anymore.

The side quests were especially disappointing. They rarely reached the same level of emotional impact, memorable storytelling, or meaningful choices. While Kingdom Come succeeds in making me feel like Henry, it rarely gave me those unforgettable moments that stay with me long after the credits roll.

Despite those flaws, I still consider Kingdom Come: Deliverance an outstanding RPG. Its immersion is second to none, and every victory truly feels earned. I just wish its quests had been as memorable as the world they were set in.

An incredible medieval simulator, but not an unforgettable storytelling experience.

Almost gave up many times trying, dying, reloading and cussing the game out. But it was worth the blood, sweat and tears. Someone mentioned "I've never seen you this intense playing a game" lol. 

If you ever did something stupid like I did, accidentally overwriting the save files with a new game (yes, this game doesn't tell you once you start a new game, it overwrites all your saves wtf), you can do this (on PC):
Go to your saves folder inside [user] > Saved Games > kingdom come, right click that folder > Properties > Previous Versions tab > Restore.

This is realism at its finest, you start as a noob literally, you can't even read, you starve and you need sleep. Oh, and did I mention you fight like a wimp? I find archery the hardest as I can't shoot ♥♥♥♥ lmao, you can put a deer right in front of me and I would've still missed it.

You can't save normally like any other games, you have to quit to save or brew some potion to save (and you have to learn the skill and recipe first). Is it worth the torture? Yes. Freaking yes.

P.S. I'm addicted to dice.

One of the most interesting RPGs out there. While there are still a lot of game-y elements in the game this has to be the most realistic game I've played without it becoming annoying.

The combat in this game is quite questionable but it is definitely something that you can get used to over time. Especially since with your skills you start out as not even being able to beat a peasant, but eventually you are able to beat several armoured opponents in a fight. Learning master strikes is a requirement though because without it you are basically done before you even started.

It has one of the most compelling characters I've ever had the pleasure of meeting and the quests are incredibly fun to do. Some of the quests can possibly hamper your enjoyment of the game though if you are not prepared for them both mentally and equipment wise. Some examples are the Monastery quest and the Pribislavitz quest.

A lot of the quests allow you to complete them in any way you can be it stealth, swords blazing, through speech or through your vanity. No matter how you build your character up there is always a way to complete a quest. Some quests also allow you to realistically think about how you would get the best possible ending for it, an example being talking to a person that doesn't even have a quest marker because you know it would be useful info to have.

The game is incredibly long taking you at least 60-80 hours to beat the game if you were to play it normally.

I do not recommend to enage with this games save system and instead to install a save anywhere mod that aren't limited to an item. While it can make combat more tense it is no fun to lose 2 hours of progress because you haven't slept in a bed.

I've spent over 180 hours on this game and most of it came from my old office PC. This game was so captivating for me, I even installed a potato graphics mod to play it at 480p, and I still had boatloads of fun. There's an obvious sense of humour throughout a lot of the side quests, but its carried out so meticulously. 

There's also a bit of janky mechanics in this game, which is quite expected for a kickstarter game, but it's nowhere near unplayable. If you've played the sequel before this, expect for a harder start and a bit of grinding early on, since even the next-door neighbour is better with his fists than the knobhead Henry.

Overall, this game was really great. I never regretted the hours I spent on it. I'd even skip fast travelling on my non-hardcore saves just to listen to the beautiful music and witness the beauty in the world. 

Grab a pitcher and enjoy this beauty!

For player of RPG games there are only two worlds - before KCD and after KCD, because after you will finish these games (KCD and KCD2) there are no other game quite like them and you will always want more...

I bought  first KCD game long after it was published and started playing it even longer after. In fact I had interupted playing AC game series and started first KCD game and it was like someone splashed you with cold water. After you are practically a sniper wíth the bow in AC Origins and demigod with melee weapons in AC Oddyssea, the KCD will bring you back to reality. You’ll find out, what is it like to be only a human who can barely draw a bow and can't hit a barn and who returns from sparring with wooden swords battered and exhausted!

First, you need to learn how to play the game itself—the rules, the mechanics, and the fact that you never get anything for free. Then your main character, Henry, has to learn everything from scratch to become a hero from a nobody, a grown man from a boy, and a mighty knight from a blacksmith’s son. And the path to achieving that is incredibly difficult, it’s challenging, it requires patience, it demands hard work, and it’s about survival - to know when to run and hide or to stand against your enemy and fight.

The life in middle ages was tough and you’ll really get a sense of just how hard it was. You’ll feel the fear when you realize your enemies—those terrifying-looking Cumans—are right behind you, that you could be robbed and killed on the road by bandits, that there are limits to how much weight you can carry and how much stamina you have, that you need to eat, sleep, and take care of your belongings, and really think through how you’ll spend your hard-earned silver groschen.
And unlike in other RPG games (most of which are fantasy, surreal, or futuristic), in the KCD world there is no magic, no supernatural force, or overpowered weapon to help you.

**Kingdom Come: Deliverance Review**

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a brilliant medieval RPG that I would highly recommend, especially if you enjoy story-driven games with deep lore, realistic world-building and strong character writing.

The graphics are very good, although I’d strongly recommend installing the HD texture pack, as it makes the world look much sharper and more detailed. The environments, villages, castles, forests and overall atmosphere all help make the game feel extremely immersive.

The story is very well written, with interesting lore surrounding both the world itself and the characters you meet throughout the journey. The character development is one of the strongest parts of the game, especially with Hans Capon. At first, he comes across as a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but over time he develops into a much more respectable and likeable character, which makes his arc feel genuinely rewarding.

The music is also very well done and adds a lot to the atmosphere. It fits the medieval setting perfectly and helps make certain moments feel more emotional, immersive and memorable.

That being said, the game is not perfect. Some missions can feel annoying, slow, or repetitive at times, and certain parts may test your patience. However, the overall experience, story, music, immersion and character writing more than make up for those flaws.

Overall, Kingdom Come: Deliverance is an excellent RPG with a strong story, interesting lore, memorable characters, great music and a believable medieval world. Despite a few frustrating missions, I would highly recommend it.
